behaviour: Reproduces the startup crash with a real prepared app and pins bootstrap, finalization, compat and wiring-error behaviour of both useRouteRef hooks.
rules: Every case sits in the existing describe 'useRouteRef during app bootstrap', so the red check `-t during.app.bootstrap` selects these cases and no others.
The describe's helpers stay as they are, apart from `finalizeApp`: `noSignInAppPlugin`, `makeTestPlugin`, `makeErrorCapture`, `makeCoreElement`, `makeFrontendElement` and `renderBootstrap`.

`finalizeApp` keeps its name, parameters and returned value. It calls `waitForFinalizedApp(preparedApp)` first, fires the optional trigger in a synchronous `act(() => { trigger?.(); })`, then runs `await act(async () => { finalizedApp = await finalizedAppPromise; })` (Gate 3, R-6). The trigger has flushed before that callback starts, so the wait cannot deadlock. Its callers do not change, and they still call `rerender(finalizedApp.element)`, the swap PreparedAppRoot does in createApp.

The new case makes finalization fail through `predicateContextLoader.load()`, the path that really reaches the catch in the finalization controller. A plugin with `pluginId: 'permission'` provides `localPermissionApiRef` through `ApiBlueprint.make`, with `factory: () => ({ authorize })` and `const authorize = jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('Permission backend unavailable'))`. That plugin also holds a root element shaped like lines 1113-1121, with `name: 'gated-element'` and `if: { permissions: { $contains: 'test.gated' } }`.

The predicate sits on that root element because a deferred root keeps its `if`: on a bootstrap-visible extension `classifyBootstrapTree` clears it before the references are collected, and finalization takes the normal path. A throwing feature flags API is no substitute: without sign-in it throws synchronously out of `onFinalized`, past the catch.

The new case does not call `rerender(finalizedApp.element)`. Its assertions read the bootstrap element that stayed mounted, because the finalized element's throwing child replaces the whole of AppRouter, root elements included, through app/root's boundary.
The new case does not assert on `finalizedApp.errors`: it is undefined on both finalization paths when nothing was collected.
Compare the error helper's result to [] as the first bootstrap assertion.
No case navigates, and each mount counter must end at exactly one call, so a remount fails the test.
Assert with `screen` and `findBy*`, in the file's `await expect(screen.findByText(...)).resolves.toBeInTheDocument()` style.

tests.name: keeps both hooks working from bootstrap through finalization

tests.expect: at bootstrap no error is posted, the texts are 'Core route: #' and 'Frontend route: none', and the link's href is '/'; after finalization both texts end in '/target', the href is '/target', and each element mounted exactly once

behaviour: Pins the core hook against a fake API carrying the lifecycle signal, and guards the legacy and signal-less behaviour that must not change.
rules: The reproducing case sits in a new describe named 'during app bootstrap', nested in the 'new app system' describe. The two guard cases sit outside it, so the red check judges the reproducing case only.

The fake API is `{ resolve, [Symbol.for('@backstage/frontend-plugin-api:route-resolution-lifecycle')]: { isFinalized, subscribe } }`. Spell the key out literally, because it pins the wire contract and U03's file does not exist when this test first runs. `subscribe` adds to a Set and returns a remover. A local `finalize()` sets the flag and calls the listeners.
Existing cases stay exactly as they are; only the listed sites change.
